message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need to know | |---------|-----------------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points are earned when you finish a round by playing all your cards. | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue) × 25 cards each (one 0, two 1–9, two “Draw Two”, two “Reverse”, two “Skip”) + 4 “Wild” + 4 “Wild Draw Four”. | | **Setup** | • Shuffle the deck.
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card to start the discard pile; if it’s a special card, follow its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a Reverse card changes direction). On your turn you may:
1. **Play** one card that matches the color, number, or symbol of the top discard, or a Wild card.
2. **Draw** one card from the draw pile if you cannot play. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | • **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – You choose the next color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise you risk a challenge.) | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, the round ends. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Draw Two/Reverse/Skip = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. First to reach the target (usually 500) wins the game. | | **House Variations** | • **“Uno” shout** – Must say “UNO” when you have one card left; failure to do so allows the next player to draw two cards.
• **“Draw 5”** – Some players use a “Draw 5” card instead of “Draw Two.”
• **“No Wild Draw Four”** – Some groups forbid Wild Draw Four to keep the game simpler. | **Quick Tips** 1. Keep track of the current color; if you’re holding a Wild, you can change the color to suit your strategy. 2. Try to play high‑value cards early to reduce the risk of opponents scoring big later. 3. Remember that “Reverse” only matters with more than two players; with two players it acts like a “Skip.” Enjoy your game!
